_doc: This repository's representations of `<module>/build/compose-previews/daemon-launch.json`,
divergences between them that are correct on purpose. Checked by
`scripts/check-daemon-launch-schema.py`. A debt register, not a config file: an entry is a
claim someone made deliberately, with the reason written down, not an exemption to add when
the check goes red.
schemaVersionSites: every place the descriptor's schema version is declared. The check fails
if any disagrees with the writer, and fails again if a `*DESCRIPTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` appears
anywhere that is not listed — a new mirror has to be declared here, which is the moment
someone can ask whether it should exist at all. The extension owns its TypeScript registry
and checks the published schema metadata for the plugin release it pins. The right long-term
number of entries here is 1: the other two are Kotlin and could read the writer's constant
directly if `:render-session-subprocess` and `:cli`
took a dependency on `:gradle-plugin:daemon-launch-builder`. Until then they are mirrors,
and mirrors need a gate rather than a comment asking a human to remember.
readerOnlyFields: a field a reader declares that the plugin's writer never emits. Each must
carry a Kotlin default, because a plugin-written descriptor will
not contain it. The check enforces that.
writerOnlyFields: a field the writer emits that a reader does not declare. Safe only while
that reader tolerates unknown keys, which the check verifies separately against the JVM
reader's `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }`.
mirroredConstants: string constants carried inside the descriptor that another module
re-declares privately. Same hazard as the schema version, one level down.
constantRegistries: qualifier -> the file declaring the constants behind it, e.g.
`DaemonProperties.Names`. A mirror that READS the shared constant instead of re-typing the
string cannot disagree with it, which is strictly better than a mirror — but the scanner then
reads `DaemonProperties.Names.SANDBOX_COUNT` where it expects a string, so the reference is
followed here and the literal behind it is what gets compared. An unregistered qualifier fails:
the gate never passes on a value it could not read.
versionStampAliases: an identifier that appears as `schemaVersion = …` at a construction site
but is not itself one of the registered constants — an indirection that forwards one. Recorded
so discovery-by-use can insist on a known name without banning the indirection.
rawKeyReaders: a reader that indexes the parsed JSON by string instead of deserialising a typed
DTO. Invisible to the structural check, and dangerous in a specific way: a missing key reads as
null rather than throwing, so a renamed field degrades into a wrong answer rather than an error.
wireFingerprint: a digest of the writer's field names, types and optionality, pinned against the
schema version it describes. Version agreement across the copies is necessary but not
sufficient — a PR could rename a field in the writer and every in-repo reader at once, leaving
all constants at v2 while a released consumer accepts the new descriptor as v2 and misreads it.
Changing the shape fails here until someone records the new digest, which is where the decision
'is this breaking?' actually gets made.
alsoAppearsIn / assumedTypes: two ways a contract escapes the Kotlin type system. The production
image passes the sandbox-count key as a literal in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, so a rename across every
Kotlin constant would still strand deployed hosts on a property nothing reads; and the doctor's
raw JSON reads have no compiler behind them, so the type each one assumes is recorded rather
than inferred.
writerEncoders: the `Json` configuration each production writer serialises through. Encoder
settings rename or drop keys without touching a declaration, so they are part of the wire
contract rather than a formatting preference.
wireFingerprint.history maps schema version -> shape digest, and entries are immutable. Changing
the shape means adding a version, never editing the digest recorded for an existing one.

schemaVersionSites.why: The source of truth. `DaemonLaunchBuilder` stamps it into every descriptor it writes, and it participates in `DaemonBootstrapTask`'s up-to-date fingerprint.

`:render-session-subprocess` writes its own descriptors for the bundle daemons it spawns, stamping this private copy, and since #5105 `SubprocessRenderSessions.open` also refuses an on-disk descriptor whose version is not this one. It is one of the twelve published contract modules an extracted preview server links against (#3824), so post-split a stale mirror here is cross-repo version skew no compiler sees.

`ServeBundleDaemon` writes its own descriptors for the bundle daemons it spawns. This entry existed until the preview server left the repository in #4732, and the `writerEncoders` note below still records its removal as a gap nothing closed. It is registered again because the render host came home (yschimke/compose-preview-server#180) — the mirror is back in a tree this check can see, so it is gated again rather than trusted. Note the spelling differs from the other two: the constant is `DAEMON_LAUNCH_SCHEMA_VERSION`, not `*_DESCRIPTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so the name-based mirror scan never finds it and only discovery-by-use does.
`compose-preview doctor` reports a descriptor written by a mismatched plugin version. Its comment already says `Keep in sync — bump together`; this makes that enforceable.

jailCommand.writtenBy: the CLI's serve path (ServeBundleDaemon.kt, ServeCommand.kt) via DaemonLaunchDescriptor.jailed()
jailCommand.why: The playground sandbox launches the daemon JVM behind an argv prefix. The Gradle plugin has no sandbox and never writes this; :daemon-client reads it when spawning. Defaults to an empty list, so a plugin-written descriptor parses unchanged.

hardTtlSeconds.writtenBy: the CLI's serve path (ServeBundleDaemon.kt, ServeCommand.kt) via DaemonLaunchDescriptor.jailed()
hardTtlSeconds.why: Wall-clock deadline after which the spawner force-kills a sandboxed daemon. Same sandbox-only origin as jailCommand; null by default.

btaCompile.why: The daemon JVM does read this config, but through flattened `composeai.daemon.bta*` system properties (DefaultBtaCompileService.fromSysprops()), not through the descriptor's nested block — so DaemonLaunchDescriptor has no reason to declare it. The VS Code extension reads the block directly to decide whether calling `compileSources` is worth a round-trip. Survivable only because the JVM reader ignores unknown keys.

SANDBOX_COUNT_PROP.why: The descriptor merges this sysprop in via `withSandboxCount()` and the daemon reads it at boot; its own KDoc says 'both sides MUST agree'. Disagreement silently gives every daemon a pool of one. The production image also passes the key as a JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS literal, but that image is yschimke/compose-preview-server's and is checked THERE, against the daemon-protocol artifact that repository resolves — the version pairing that actually ships. Checking it from here would compare two default branches instead.

schemaVersion.why: `DaemonBootstrapTask.schemaVersion`, an `@Input` property whose getter returns DAEMON_DESCRIPTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION. The indirection is deliberate: it puts the version into the task's up-to-date fingerprint so a bump re-runs the task. Scoped to this file — a bare name would let any writer's local `schemaVersion` through.

cli/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/composeai.why: `compose-preview doctor` parses the descriptor to a JsonObject and indexes it by string (`enabled`, `schemaVersion`, `javaLauncher`, `manifestPath`) so it can report on a descriptor a typed reader would reject outright. A key that no longer exists reads as null, so doctor would quietly report the daemon disabled instead of failing.

wireFingerprint.why: The shape of the descriptor AS EMITTED, recorded per schema version: the writer's DTO, the DTOs it nests, and the reader-only fields a registered writer actually puts on the wire (serve's jailCommand / hardTtlSeconds). A version's entry is IMMUTABLE once written — changing the shape means adding a version, not refreshing this one.

writerEncoders.why: Every production writer's `Json`, recorded per file because they are not identical. The two Gradle-plugin writers pretty-print and force explicit nulls. The settings that DO change the wire (a `namingStrategy`, or `encodeDefaults = false` dropping defaulted fields) live in the same block, so they are recorded rather than assumed. Serve's writer (`ServeBundleDaemon`, compact, relying on kotlinx's `explicitNulls = true` default) was registered here, then left with the server in #4732, and is registered again now that the render host came home (yschimke/compose-preview-server#180). It is deliberately NOT identical to the two Gradle-plugin writers: it does not pretty-print, and it leans on kotlinx's `explicitNulls = true` default rather than stating it. Both are recorded rather than normalised, because this block exists to make the differences visible, not to assert they should not exist. Residual item 1 on #4732 — that a shape change here no longer fails the server's build — is narrowed rather than closed: the writer is gated again, but the server's own image still passes descriptor keys this check cannot see.
